name: Pherkad
description: A star 149 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75097: radius 16.408 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 998.14 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.058) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75097: effective temperature 8015 +/- 240 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.042)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75097: distance 149.254 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.016), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 149 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 998 times the Sun's luminosity at 8,015 K, so 16.408 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 75097: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Pherkad
quotes.card: Pherkad, Bayer designation Gamma Ursae Minoris, is a star in the northern constellation of Ursa Minor.
quotes.introduction: Together with Beta Ursae Minoris (Kochab), it forms the end of the dipper pan of the "Little Dipper", which is an asterism forming the tail of the bear.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1696877570753454208 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
